text: James Joyce's Ulysses was declared obscene by a U.S. court while it was being published serially in The Little Review, from 1918 until 1920. In October 1922 the New York Post Office Authorities seized and burned 500 copies during an attempt to import the novel into the United States, where its certification as obscene made importation illegal. On May 8, 1933, United States Customs seized a copy imported by Random House in New York as pornographic; on December 6, 1933, Judge John M. Woolsey denied the government's motion for forfeiture and destruction.
meta_description: Ulysses by James Joyce: declared obscene by a U.S. court, 500 copies burned in 1922, cleared by Judge Woolsey in 1933.
